ReflexiveModel

class ReflexiveModel[source]

Bases: object

Mixin with set_data/get_data based on PROPERTIES.

Subclasses (dataclasses decorated with initialize_reflexive) declare in REF_PROPERTIES the fields that reference another model: in get_data they become the id of the referenced object (or None). Enum values become their value.

Attributes:
PROPERTIESClassVar[list[str]], class attribute

Field names of the model, filled by initialize_reflexive.

DATA_PROPERTIESClassVar[list], class attribute

Default value of each init field, filled by initialize_reflexive.

REF_PROPERTIESClassVar[tuple[str, …]], class attribute

Fields that reference another model. Empty by default.

Examples

>>> from dataclasses import dataclass
>>> from types import SimpleNamespace
>>> @initialize_reflexive
... @dataclass
... class Item(ReflexiveModel):
...     id: int
...     owner: object
...     REF_PROPERTIES = ("owner",)
>>> item = Item(id=7, owner=SimpleNamespace(id=3))
>>> item.get_data()
[{'id': 7, 'owner': 3}]
>>> item.set_data({"id": 8, "unknown": 1})
>>> item.id
8

Methods

get_data

Return the model data as a list with one dictionary.

set_data

Update attributes from a dictionary.
set_data(data)[source]

Update attributes from a dictionary.

Parameters:
datadict

New values, keyed by field name.

Notes

Only keys present in PROPERTIES are applied; other keys are ignored. No validation or type conversion is performed on the input data.

get_data()[source]

Return the model data as a list with one dictionary.

Returns:
list[dict]

A single dictionary with one entry per field of PROPERTIES. A list is returned for consistency with potential multi-record returns.

Notes

  • References (REF_PROPERTIES) are replaced by their id. A value without id (e.g. text already read from the CSV) is kept as is, and a falsy value (None, 0, “”) becomes None.

  • Enum values are replaced by their value.

Examples

>>> from dataclasses import dataclass
>>> @initialize_reflexive
... @dataclass
... class Item(ReflexiveModel):
...     id: int
...     owner: object
...     REF_PROPERTIES = ("owner",)
>>> Item(id=7, owner="3").get_data()
[{'id': 7, 'owner': '3'}]
>>> Item(id=7, owner=None).get_data()
[{'id': 7, 'owner': None}]
